Elite anchor – Staff Machine Learning Engineer (rare_air 92–96)
ELENA PARK
Staff Machine Learning Engineer
Seattle, WA • elena.park@example.com • (555) 555-0181 • github.com/elenapark • linkedin.com/in/elenapark

SUMMARY
Staff-level ML engineer specializing in large scale recommendation and ranking systems. Ten plus years experience shipping models to hundreds of millions of users, with a track record of improving revenue, engagement, and infra efficiency. Strong at partnering with product, infra, and data science to turn ambiguous problems into measurable wins.

EXPERIENCE

Staff Machine Learning Engineer – Personalization
Nimbus Streaming – Seattle, WA
Jan 2020 – Present

Tech lead for the home feed and recommendations stack for a 200M monthly active user streaming platform.

Designed and deployed a new two stage ranking architecture (candidate generation plus learned re ranking) that increased weekly watch time by 11 percent and subscription conversion by 6 percent while holding infra cost flat.

Led migration from legacy gradient boosted trees to a deep learning model (Wide and Deep with attention features), improving AUC by 4 points and reducing cold start error rates by 18 percent.

Partnered with infra to introduce an embedding service and feature store, cutting model feature latency by 40 percent and training pipeline time by 35 percent.

Mentored a team of 6 ML engineers and 3 data scientists, driving a culture of clear experiment design, readable dashboards, and defensible decision memos.

Drove fairness and quality reviews for personalization models, tightening guardrails on extreme content and establishing a quarterly model audit process with Legal and Policy.

Senior Machine Learning Engineer – Ads Quality
Nimbus Streaming – Seattle, WA
Aug 2015 – Dec 2019

Owned click through rate and conversion prediction models for a 1B plus daily request ads platform.

Introduced calibrated probability outputs and better down funnel metrics, enabling sales and finance to price inventory more accurately and unlocking an estimated 22 million dollars per year in net new revenue.

Built a reusable offline evaluation harness that cut iteration time from weeks to days, increasing the number of experiments per quarter by 3 times.

Partnered with infra to define SLAs and SLOs for serving models, reducing P95 latency by 25 percent and cutting timeouts by 40 percent.

Mentored junior engineers on feature engineering, experiment design, and production rollouts.

Machine Learning Engineer
Nimbus Retail – San Francisco, CA
Jul 2012 – Jul 2015

Built and shipped demand forecasting models that reduced stock outs by 17 percent and excess inventory by 9 percent across three major product categories.

Collaborated with supply chain and operations to integrate forecasts into purchasing workflows, reducing manual overrides by 30 percent.

Maintained model performance and data pipelines in production, including monitoring, retraining, and incident response.

EDUCATION

M.S. Computer Science, Machine Learning focus
University of Washington – Seattle, WA

B.S. Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
University of California, Berkeley

SKILLS

Languages: Python, SQL, Scala

ML: PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost, scikit-learn

Systems: Kafka, Airflow, Kubernetes, Redis, gRPC

Domains: ranking, recommendations, ads quality, experimentation, causal inference

Practices: A B testing, offline evaluation, model monitoring, technical leadership, mentoring

OTHER LINE REWRITES

Useful edits, kept with their own source.

These do not map uniquely to the ranked fixes above, so each stays beside the exact line it rewrites.

LINE EDIT 01 · SOURCE LINE

“Drove fairness and quality reviews for personalization models, tightening guardrails on extreme content and establishing a quarterly model audit process with Legal and Policy.”

REWRITE

Drove fairness and quality reviews for personalization models, tightening guardrails on extreme content and establishing a quarterly model audit process with Legal and Policy; scope: [specific scope]; outcome: [measurable result].

Add the number of models, review findings, or launch decisions affected to show what the audit process changed.

LINE EDIT 02 · SOURCE LINE

“Mentored a team of 6 ML engineers and 3 data scientists, driving a culture of clear experiment design, readable dashboards, and defensible decision memos.”

REWRITE

Mentored a team of 6 ML engineers and 3 data scientists by setting expectations for experiment design, readable dashboards, and defensible decision memos; [team or delivery improvement].

Add one verified change in team practice, delivery cadence, or decision quality to make the mentoring work concrete.

QUESTIONS WORTH ANSWERING

Prompts for your next revision.

These questions are not tied to a specific ranked fix. Use whichever ones surface a true, useful detail.

QUESTION 01

When did watch time and subscription conversion move differently, and how did you choose the ranking tradeoff?

Why it may help: Your ranking work reports both measures, but the decision tension between them is not visible.

QUESTION 02

What changed in the architecture or operating model to serve a 200M monthly active user platform?

Why it may help: The user scale is clear; the engineering choices that made it workable would sharpen the Staff-level story.

QUESTION 03

Describe a personalization incident where guardrails, latency, or model quality forced a difficult production decision.

Why it may help: The resume names monitoring and fairness reviews, but not a concrete high-pressure judgment.

QUESTION 04

Which part of the offline evaluation harness removed the most iteration time from weeks to days?

Why it may help: The time reduction is strong, and explaining the mechanism would make the improvement more transferable.

QUESTION 05

How did Legal and Policy change the quarterly personalization audit process or its launch decisions?

Why it may help: The partnership is named, but the practical consequence of that collaboration is not stated.

KEEP THESE

The parts already earning trust.
01

The two-stage ranking architecture connects candidate generation and learned re-ranking to 11 percent more weekly watch time, 6 percent higher subscription conversion, and flat infrastructure cost.

02

The ads quality role links calibrated probabilities and down-funnel metrics to an estimated 22 million dollars per year in net new revenue, which makes the business value easy to understand.

03

The career progression from demand forecasting to ads quality to personalization shows a consistent production ML path across retail, advertising, and streaming.

ROLE DIRECTION

Where this story reads strongest.

Position yourself around large-scale ranking and recommendation systems with unusually clear business and infrastructure results. For Staff or Principal ML roles, bring the leadership decisions and cross-functional operating model closer to the foreground.
